L2708@P35: Algebraic spaces were introduced by Artin [Ar68, §1], and the theory developed by himself and his student Knutson [Kn71]. The spaces are constructed by
L2709@P35: gluing together schemes along open subsets that are isomorphic locally in the ´etale
L2710@P35: topology. Over C, these open sets are locally analytically isomorphic; so an algebraic space is a kind of complex analytic space. In general and more formally, an
L2711@P35: algebraic space is the quotient in the category of ´etale sheaves of a scheme divided
L2712@P35: by an ´etale equivalence relation.
L2713@P35: Artin [Ar67, Thm. 3.4, p. 35], proceeding in the spirit of Grothendieck and
L2714@P35: Murre, identified five conditions on a functor that are necessary and sufficient for it
L2715@P35: to be a locally separated algebraic space that is locally of finite type over a field or
L2716@P35: over an excellent Dedekind domain. In the proof of necessity, a key new ingredient
L2717@P35: is Artin’s approximation theorem; it implies that the topological rings given by prorepresentability can be algebraized. The resulting schemes are then glued together
L2718@P35: via an ´etale equivalence relation.
L2719@P35: By checking that the five conditions hold, Artin [Ar67, Thm. 7.3, p. 67] proved
L2720@P35: the following theorem.
